text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

Before I draft this, there's a problem with the main promise and a few things I need from you.

**The "same cleaner every single time" promise.** Your new system is a regular cleaner plus a named backup. That means some visits will be done by the backup. And with 7 of 18 cleaners leaving last year, you can't guarantee anyone stays. Cleaner changes were the second most common reason people left, so these readers will notice if the promise breaks. I'd suggest something you can keep, like: "You'll have your own regular cleaner, plus a named backup you'll meet ahead of time, never a stranger." Does that work, or is there something else that would make "every time" true?

My other questions:

1. **Is anything different for cleaners now?** For example, a raise, better hours or less turnover so far this year. If so, I can say "your cleaner is more likely to stay," not just "we've changed how we assign people."
2. **Does the $99 first cleaning have conditions?** Is there a deadline, or does it require booking every-other-week service after that?
3. **What does the reader actually get for the extra $25?** Should I name the $140 apps directly, or just say what you do differently (employees, insurance on every visit) without comparing?
4. **Who signs it, and how do people rebook?** Your name and title, plus a link, phone number or "reply to this email."

You're right, I can't promise every single time because of sick days and holidays. Your wording works, just make it as strong as you can without being false.

1. Since we started giving each customer a regular cleaner in July, only 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.
2. The $99 offer ends December 31. There's no contract, so they can cancel any time.
3. Our cleaners are employees with insurance on every visit. The app services around here mostly use contractors with no insurance on the visit. I can't match $140. I don't have a preference on naming the apps, so do whatever you think works best.
4. Lisa Grant, Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning. They can book by replying to the email or calling 555-0164.

I didn't name any app companies. Naming them would invite a comparison and wouldn't make your case stronger.

Subject: Your own cleaner, and $99 to come back

Hi [First name],

When customers left us last year, the reasons we heard most were price and a different cleaner showing up too often. We've worked on both.

Since July, every customer has their own regular cleaner, plus a named backup for sick days and holidays. You'll always know who's coming. Since then, only 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.

We'll be straight about price. An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom home is $165 with us. App services nearby charge about $140. The difference pays for cleaners who are our employees, earning $21 an hour, with insurance on every visit. Most app services use contractors with no insurance on the visit.

Come back before December 31 and your first cleaning is $99. There's no contract, and you can cancel any time.

Reply to this email or call 555-0164 to book.

Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

A few notes:

- **The backup.** Earlier I suggested saying customers would meet their backup ahead of time. I left that out because you didn't tell me it happens. If it does, adding "you'll meet your backup in advance" would make the email stronger.
- **The 3-bedroom price.** If you have customers with smaller or larger homes, consider adding "for example" before the price so it doesn't read as their quote.
- **The cleaner numbers.** "Only 1 of 18 since July" is true, but it covers just four months. Keep using that line only while it stays true.
